doc: one numbered rule for a skill that tells a reviewer how to test an agent skill. Give it a bold title that says what to do, followed by its body.
notes: Skill runs can be contaminated: the user's global settings can reach a run, and the skill's reference files can be unreadable if the directory wasn't added.
The reviewer has to use the run's log to check before believing the run.
When these go wrong the final answer looks perfectly normal, so reading the answer won't reveal it.
This came up in the review of a skill called operate on 2026-11-01.
facts: The reviewer must confirm before trusting a run
The confirmation comes from the run's log
Other instructions, such as the user's global settings, must not have reached the run
The agent must have been able to read the skill's reference files
A failure of either kind leaves the answer looking normal

doc: a git commit message, with a subject line and a body.
notes: The file skills/skill-review/references/running-a-skill.md told reviewers to check whether a run got a shell through a subagent.
We tested on Claude Code 2.1.310: under --disallowedTools Bash, a general-purpose subagent had no Bash tool in 4 of 4 runs.
Without the flag and with the command allowed, a subagent ran the command in 1 of 1 runs.
The reference now says the flag also covers subagents and the check was removed.
Results are written up in docs/context/skill-review-lessons.md.
facts: The reference now says the flag covers subagents
The earlier instruction to check for a shell through a subagent is gone
The test was on Claude Code 2.1.310

doc: a pull request description for a reviewer who has to decide whether to merge it.
notes: The change records a decision that a skill's rule-bearing sections are capped at fifty lines instead of the whole file being capped at seventy.
The old limit, decision 0009, counted the whole file by wc -l, so the frontmatter and footer used up room meant for rules.
Frontmatter, title, purpose, the Not here section, footer and footnotes are no longer counted.
Measured 2026-10-28: the most rule-bearing lines in any skill is 48 (procedures), then 46 (steward), then 44 (contracts).
No skill needs changing to meet the new cap.
There is no automatic check yet; the limit is enforced in review.
The count can be reproduced with an awk command given in the record, docs/decisions/0031-fifty-lines-of-rules.md.
facts: The cap moves from seventy lines for the whole file to fifty lines of rule-bearing sections
Frontmatter, title, purpose, Not here, footer and footnotes aren't counted
The highest current count is 48 lines (procedures)
No skill has to change
Enforcement is in review, with no automatic check
The record is docs/decisions/0031-fifty-lines-of-rules.md

doc: a README section telling a developer how to try a skill library in Claude Code without installing it for good.
notes: The library is a plugin directory; its manifest is at .claude-plugin/plugin.json.
Clone the repository, then start Claude Code with claude --plugin-dir pointing at the clone.
That makes the skills available for that session only; nothing is installed permanently.
Skills load on their own when the task matches their description; you can check by asking for a task and watching for a Skill tool call.
Reference files sit under each skill's references/ directory, and you may need --add-dir with the same path for an agent to read them when the clone is outside your project.
facts: Clone the repository
Start Claude Code with --plugin-dir pointing at the clone
It lasts for that session only
Skills load when the task matches their description
--add-dir may be needed so reference files can be read when the clone is outside the project

doc: a short documentation page on how to compare what an agent does with and without a skill.
notes: Create a new throwaway directory holding only what the task needs.
Add a .claude/settings.json with claudeMdExcludes for the user's global CLAUDE.md, because --setting-sources project alone doesn't keep it out.
Run claude -p with the same prompt twice, changing nothing else: once with --plugin-dir and --add-dir set to the plugin, once without them.
Use --output-format stream-json --verbose and save each to a file.
Without --add-dir, reads of reference files are refused and the run carries on as if nothing happened.
In the log, check the init entry for what was available, Skill tool_use entries for whether the skill loaded, and permission_denials in the final result entry for refused reads or writes.
Check the log before reading the answer.
facts: Use a new directory holding only what the task needs
claudeMdExcludes is needed, because --setting-sources project alone doesn't exclude the global file
Run the same prompt twice, with and without the plugin
--add-dir is needed or reference reads are silently refused
Save stream-json logs
Check the init entry, Skill tool_use entries and permission_denials
Check the log before reading the answer
